+"""One finding format for every review bot."""
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Finding:
+    bot: str
+    path: str
+    start_line: int
+    end_line: int
+    body: str
+    severity: str = "unknown"
+    sources: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+def from_review_comment(bot: str, c: dict) -> Finding:
+    """Build a Finding from a GitHub pull request review comment (REST API shape)."""
+    end = c.get("line") or c.get("original_line")
body:
`end` can be `None` here (GitHub review comments have null `line`/`original_line` for file-level or outdated comments), which then flows into `Finding.start_line`/`end_line` as `None`. That silently breaks `overlaps()` later with a `TypeError` when it does `a.start_line - slack`. Either reject/skip such comments explicitly or default the lines, e.g.:

```python
    end = c.get("line") or c.get("original_line") or 0
    start = c.get("start_line") or c.get("original_start_line") or end
```

Falling back to `original_start_line` also keeps multi-line comments consistent when only the original position data is present.

+"""One finding format for every review bot."""
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Finding:

+def from_review_comment(bot: str, c: dict) -> Finding:
+    """Build a Finding from a GitHub pull request review comment (REST API shape)."""
+    end = c.get("line") or c.get("original_line")
+    start = c.get("start_line") or end
+    return Finding(bot=bot, path=c["path"], start_line=start, end_line=end,
+                   body=c["body"], sources=[c["html_url"]])
+
+
+def overlaps(a: Finding, b: Finding, slack: int = 3) -> bool:
+    """True when two findings point at the same file and nearby lines."""
+    return a.path == b.path and a.start_line - slack <= b.end_line and b.start_line - slack <= a.end_line
body:
Line-number overlap alone can produce false duplicates when two findings sit on the same line number but different diff sides (e.g. a deletion on LEFT vs an addition on RIGHT at line 15, or comments on different commits/sha of the same PR). Consider carrying the diff `side` (and maybe the commit `sha`) on `Finding` and requiring it to match in `overlaps()` before comparing lines. Fine to defer if the normalizer only ever sees one side, but worth deciding now since this type is meant to be the shared format across all bots.

body:
`line` is the position in the PR's *current* head, while `original_line` is the position in the commit where the review was made. Falling back to `original_line` means a Finding's line number may refer to a stale diff: if the branch is force-pushed/rebased between two bots' reviews, `overlaps()` will compare line numbers from different versions of the file and dedupe (or fail to dedupe) incorrectly. Consider consistently preferring `line`, and either skipping comments where only `original_line` exists or recording the commit (`c["commit_id"]`) / a "stale" flag on the Finding so `overlaps()` can decline to compare stale findings.

+    return a.path == b.path and a.start_line - slack <= b.end_line and b.start_line - slack <= a.end_line
body:
`overlaps()` only checks `path` + line proximity. GitHub review comments also have `side`/`original_side` (`LEFT` = old code, `RIGHT` = new code). Two comments at line 10 on opposite sides of the diff are about *different* code but will be treated as duplicates. Consider adding `side` to `Finding` and requiring it to match:

```python
def overlaps(a: Finding, b: Finding, slack: int = 3) -> bool:
    return (a.path == b.path and a.side == b.side
            and a.start_line - slack <= b.end_line
            and b.start_line - slack <= a.end_line)
```

body:
`end` and `start` can be `None` for comments that carry no line info — e.g. file-level review comments, replies (`in_reply_to_id` set, no `line`), or some webhook payloads. The `Finding` type declares `start_line`/`end_line` as `int`, but a `None` slips through and later crashes `overlaps()` with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'NoneType' and 'int'`. Also note `or` treats `0` as missing (not an issue for 1-based GitHub lines, but worth being explicit). Suggest failing fast or handling it deliberately:

```python
end = c.get("line") or c.get("original_line")
if end is None:
    raise ValueError(f"comment {c.get('html_url')} has no line info")
start = c.get("start_line") or end
```

Alternatively, add a sentinel (e.g. `start_line = end_line = -1`) for file-level findings and make `overlaps` treat those specially, but silently returning an invalid `Finding` is the worst of the options.
